article.h1: PMEGP Scheme 2026: Complete Guide to Eligibility, Subsidy & Application
article.snippetAnswer: The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) is a credit-linked subsidy scheme administered by the Ministry of MSME and implemented nationally by KVIC to establish new micro-enterprises. It offers maximum eligible project costs of ₹50 lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for service/business units. General category beneficiaries receive 15% (urban) or 25% (rural) subsidy with 10% contribution, while special category beneficiaries receive 25% (urban) or 35% (rural) subsidy with 5% contribution. Online applications are accepted via kviconline.gov.in.

schemeAtAGlance.Administering Ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME)

article.introduction: The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) is a flagship credit-linked subsidy scheme initiated by the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) to generate employment opportunities by establishing new micro-enterprises in non-farm sectors across India.
article.whatIsScheme: PMEGP is a financial assistance initiative administered at the national level by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) as the single nodal agency, with state-level implementation through KVIC directorates, State KVIBs, District Industries Centres (DICs), and Coir Board. It provides margin money subsidies directly linked to bank credit.

detailedExplanation.heading: Project Cost Ceilings & Sectoral Limits
detailedExplanation.text: PMEGP clearly distinguishes project cost limits by sector. Under the revised guidelines, the maximum eligible project cost for manufacturing sector micro-enterprises is ₹50 lakh. For service and business sector projects, the maximum eligible project cost is ₹20 lakh. Sanctioned project amounts above these ceiling limits are funded through bank credit, but margin money subsidy calculation is capped strictly at ₹50 lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for service units.

detailedExplanation.heading: Subsidy & Beneficiary Contribution Structure
detailedExplanation.text: Margin money subsidy varies according to beneficiary category and project location. General Category applicants in urban areas receive a 15% subsidy with a 10% own contribution, while in rural areas they receive a 25% subsidy with a 10% contribution. Special Category beneficiaries (SC, ST, OBC, Minorities, Women, Ex-Servicemen, Differently Abled, NER, Hill & Border areas) in urban areas receive a 25% subsidy with a 5% contribution, while in rural areas they receive a 35% subsidy with a 5% contribution.

detailedExplanation.heading: Eligibility Distinction: New Enterprises vs Upgradation
detailedExplanation.text: Standard PMEGP assistance is strictly for setting up NEW micro-enterprises. Existing units or projects that have already availed government subsidy under any other Central or State scheme are ineligible for standard PMEGP. A separate second loan component for existing well-performing PMEGP/REGP/MUDRA units offers upgradation assistance up to ₹1 crore for manufacturing and ₹25 lakh for service with a 15-20% subsidy.

keyBenefits.title: Substantial Margin Money Subsidy
keyBenefits.description: Up to 35% subsidy for special category beneficiaries in rural areas and 25% in urban areas.

keyBenefits.title: Sector-Specific Financial Ceilings
keyBenefits.description: Financial support for manufacturing projects up to ₹50 lakh and service projects up to ₹20 lakh.

keyBenefits.title: Low Beneficiary Contribution Requirement
keyBenefits.description: Requires only 5% own contribution for special categories and 10% for general category applicants.

keyBenefits.title: Collateral-Free Bank Financing
keyBenefits.description: Bank loans up to ₹10 lakh are covered under CGTMSE without mandatory collateral security.

keyBenefits.title: Structured EDP Training Support
keyBenefits.description: Mandatory Entrepreneurship Development Programme training provided to equip entrepreneurs for business success.

eligibility.criteria: Minimum 18 years of age (no upper age limit).
At least 8th pass for manufacturing projects above ₹10 lakh and service projects above ₹5 lakh.
Individuals, Self Help Groups, Registered Societies, and Charitable Trusts.
Assistance is strictly for setting up NEW micro-enterprises; existing subsidized units are ineligible for first-stage PMEGP.
No upper income ceiling for establishing new units under PMEGP.

documentsRequired.purpose: Business Plan and Financial Outlay Assessment
Proof of 8th Pass (for manufacturing > ₹10 lakh / service > ₹5 lakh)
Proof for 25%-35% Special Category Subsidy Claim
Proof of project location in rural area for higher subsidy

applicationProcess: Visit the official PMEGP e-portal at kviconline.gov.in
Click on PMEGP Application Form for Individual or Non-Individual category
Fill in personal, bank, agency, and project details
Upload required Aadhaar, DPR, education, and category documents
Submit the online application and track status via Scorecard ID
mistakesToAvoid: Applying for an existing business under the standard new-unit PMEGP scheme
Failing to submit the 8th pass certificate for manufacturing projects exceeding ₹10 lakh
Selecting an incorrect implementing agency or DIC location during portal registration

faqs.question: What is the maximum project cost allowed under PMEGP?
faqs.answer: The maximum eligible project cost is ₹50 lakh for manufacturing sector projects and ₹20 lakh for service/business sector projects under PMEGP guidelines.

faqs.question: Who administers and implements the PMEGP scheme?
faqs.answer: PMEGP is administered by the Ministry of MSME and implemented nationally by Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) as the single nodal agency, alongside KVIB, DIC, and Coir Board.

faqs.question: What is the subsidy rate for general category applicants?
faqs.answer: General category applicants receive a 15% subsidy in urban areas and a 25% subsidy in rural areas, with a mandatory 10% own contribution.

faqs.question: What is the subsidy rate for special category beneficiaries?
faqs.answer: Special category beneficiaries (SC, ST, OBC, Minorities, Women, Ex-Servicemen, PH) receive a 25% subsidy in urban areas and a 35% subsidy in rural areas, with a 5% contribution.

faqs.question: Can existing businesses apply for standard PMEGP loans?
faqs.answer: No. Standard PMEGP is strictly for setting up new micro-enterprises. However, existing well-performing units can apply for a separate second loan for expansion/upgradation.

faqs.question: Is 8th pass mandatory for all PMEGP applications?
faqs.answer: Education qualification of 8th pass is mandatory only if project cost exceeds ₹10 lakh in manufacturing sector or ₹5 lakh in service sector.

faqs.question: Is there an income limit to apply for PMEGP?
faqs.answer: No. There is no upper income limit for individuals establishing new projects under PMEGP.

faqs.question: How is the PMEGP application submitted?
faqs.answer: PMEGP applications are submitted strictly online through the official portal at kviconline.gov.in.

faqs.question: Is collateral security required for PMEGP loans?
faqs.answer: No collateral security is required for project loans up to ₹10 lakh under CGTMSE coverage.

faqs.question: What is the minimum age requirement for PMEGP?
faqs.answer: The applicant must be at least 18 years of age at the time of application.

faqs.question: What happens if a project cost exceeds ₹50 lakh in manufacturing?
faqs.answer: Bank credit can fund project costs above ₹50 lakh, but the maximum margin money subsidy calculation is strictly capped at ₹50 lakh.

faqs.question: What is the duration of EDP training under PMEGP?
faqs.answer: Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) training is mandatory for selected beneficiaries prior to subsidy release.

faqs.question: Which agencies accept offline PMEGP physical forms?
faqs.answer: No physical application forms are accepted; all applications must be filed on kviconline.gov.in.

faqs.question: Can SHGs or Charitable Trusts apply for PMEGP?
faqs.answer: Yes. Self Help Groups, Registered Societies, and Charitable Trusts are eligible to apply under PMEGP.

faqs.question: What is the lock-in period for PMEGP margin money subsidy?
faqs.answer: The margin money subsidy is kept in a term deposit account for a lock-in period of 3 years by the financing bank branch.

article.conclusion: The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) remains India's premier credit-linked subsidy scheme for aspiring micro-entrepreneurs in both rural and urban areas. By offering up to 35% margin money subsidy and credit support up to ₹50 lakh, PMEGP effectively removes capital barriers for setting up new enterprises. For assistance with eligibility assessment, documentation or scheme application planning, you can consult Growthora.
